title: Package Delivery
statementMd:
Johnny drives a truck and must deliver a package from his hometown to the district center. His hometown is located at point $0$ on a number line, and the district center is located at the point $*d*$.

Johnny's truck has a gas tank that holds exactly $*n*$ liters, and his tank is initially full. As he drives, the truck consumes exactly one liter per unit distance traveled. Moreover, there are $*m*$ gas stations located at various points along the way to the district center. The $*i*$-th station is located at the point $*x*_{*i*}$ on the number line and sells an unlimited amount of fuel at a price of $*p*_{*i*}$ dollars per liter. Find the minimum cost Johnny must pay for fuel to successfully complete the delivery.

## Input

The first line of input contains three space separated integers $*d*$, $*n*$, and $*m*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ *d* ≤ 10^{9}$, $1 ≤ *m* ≤ 200 000$) — the total distance to the district center, the volume of the gas tank, and the number of gas stations, respectively.

Each of the next $*m*$ lines contains two integers $*x*_{*i*}$, $*p*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *x*_{*i*} ≤ *d* - 1$, $1 ≤ *p*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{6}$) — the position and cost of gas at the $*i*$-th gas station. It is guaranteed that the positions of the gas stations are distinct.

## Output

Print a single integer — the minimum cost to complete the delivery. If there is no way to complete the delivery, print `-1`.

## Note

In the first sample, Johnny's truck holds $4$ liters. He can drive $3$ units to the first gas station, buy $2$ liters of gas there (bringing the tank to $3$ liters total), drive $3$ more units to the third gas station, buy $4$ liters there to fill up his tank, and then drive straight to the district center. His total cost is $2·5 + 4·3 = 22$ dollars.

In the second sample, there is no way for Johnny to make it to the district center, as his tank cannot hold enough gas to take him from the latest gas station to the district center.
statementZhMd:
Johnny 驾驶一辆卡车，必须将一个包裹从他的家乡运送到地区中心。他的家乡位于数轴上的点 $0$，地区中心位于点 $*d*$。

Johnny 的卡车油箱最多可装恰好 $*n*$ 升汽油，出发时油箱已加满。卡车行驶时，每行驶一个单位距离恰好消耗一升汽油。此外，从家乡到地区中心的沿途有 $*m*$ 个加油站，分别位于数轴上的不同位置。第 $*i*$ 个加油站位于点 $*x*_{*i*}$，以每升 $*p*_{*i*}$ 美元的价格出售不限量的汽油。请计算 Johnny 为成功完成运输任务所需支付的最小燃油费用。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含三个由空格分隔的整数 $*d*$、$*n*$ 和 $*m*$（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ *d* ≤ 10^{9}$，$1 ≤ *m* ≤ 200 000$），分别表示到地区中心的总距离、油箱容量以及加油站的数量。

接下来的 $*m*$ 行中，每行包含两个整数 $*x*_{*i*}$、$*p*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *x*_{*i*} ≤ *d* - 1$，$1 ≤ *p*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{6}$），分别表示第 $*i*$ 个加油站的位置和汽油价格。保证所有加油站的位置各不相同。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数，即完成运输任务所需支付的最小费用。如果无法完成运输任务，输出 `-1`。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，Johnny 的卡车可以装 $4$ 升汽油。他可以先行驶 $3$ 个单位距离到达第一个加油站，在那里购买 $2$ 升汽油，使油箱中共有 $3$ 升汽油；然后再行驶 $3$ 个单位距离到达第三个加油站，在那里购买 $4$ 升汽油以加满油箱，最后直接驶向地区中心。他支付的总费用为 $2·5 + 4·3 = 22$ 美元。

在第二个样例中，Johnny 无法到达地区中心，因为他的油箱无法装下从最后一个加油站前往地区中心所需的足够汽油。
